title: 72-year-old Palestinian woman shot and killed by Israeli settlers near newly established outpost | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A 72-year-old Palestinian woman was shot and killed by Israeli settlers in front of her home in the occupiedWest Bankon Tuesday, according to Palestinian officials and eyewitnesses.

Fadda Fuhaidat was shot in the head after midnight near the city of Jericho, where Israeli settlers took over eight Palestinian homes two weeks ago.

Fuhaidat’s 19-year-old granddaughter, Nagham, told CNN the Israeli settlers have been harassing residents in the area since moving in.

The incident on Tuesday began when settlers illegally drove into Area A in the West Bank, which is territory where Israeli civilians are prohibited from entering. But how the shooting unfolded is in dispute and remains under Israeli police investigation, as well as a review from Israel Defense Forces (IDF) commanders.

According to Nagham, a group of armed settlers came toward their neighborhood and began firing indiscriminately late Monday evening. Six Palestinians were shot and injured, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry.

Nagham said her mother called her husband, Arafat, and asked him to come help. Arafat sped over and hit the settlers’ car by accident, Nagham said. As Arafat stepped out of his car, he was shot in the leg and required medical attention, she said.

When Fuhaidat heard gunshots, she ran into the street to see what was happening. A bullet struck her in the back of the head, Nagham said, killing her in front of her home.

According to an Israeli military official, a Palestinian car struck the vehicle with Israeli settlers, sparking an argument that quickly escalated. Several additional Israelis and Palestinians arrived at the scene, the official said. As Palestinians threw stones at the Israelis, the official said Israeli settlers fired shots at the Palestinians. One of the bullets from an Israeli settler killed Fuhaidat, the official said.

Two weeks ago, dozens of Israeli settlers moved into homes in this area with the backing of the settler organization Nachala and the Binyamin Regional Council, which claimed the homes were purchased.

After settlers moved into the homes, the head of the Binyamin Regional Council Israel Ganz said, “We are dismantling the Oslo Accords through action, house by house, family by family.”

The Oslo Accords, signed in 1993 between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), were designed to pave the way for the establishment of a Palestinian state and the realization of a two-state solution.

The IDF said it took two Palestinians into custody after the incident — Arafat and his son, according to Nagham — accusing them of “the deliberate collision and attack on the Israelis.” No Israeli settlers were arrested, the Israeli military official said.

Nagham said that settlers stayed in the area and blocked ambulances from reaching the injured.

“It is a clear false claim … why did the army protect the settlers? They should get arrested, not us. We didn’t do anything wrong,” Nagham said.

CNN’s Dana Karni contributed to this report

CNN’s Dana Karni contributed to this report
